records.name: St. Martin of Tours Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Roosevelt Boulevard and Cheltenham Avenue with Masses in Q'eqchi, Spanish and English, and Saturday evening Masses for its Brazilian and Neocatechumenal Way communities.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in the language you follow, or join the Thursday adoration, which runs after the 8:30 am Mass until 6:30 pm and ends with the rosary. The parish also lists a Brazilian apostolate, a Portuguese apostolate and a Neocatechumenal Way Mass, but the listings give no meeting times or contacts for the groups themselves.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 7 am in Q'eqchi, 10 am in Spanish and noon in English. Saturday Mass at 4 pm, and at 7:30 pm for the Brazilian and Neocatechumenal Way groups. Weekday Mass at 8:30 am, and Thursday adoration after the 8:30 am Mass until 6:30 pm. Saturday confession 3 to 3:45 pm.

first_step.how: Go to the 10 am Spanish Mass or the noon English Mass on Sunday, where no sign-up is listed. Call the rectory at 215-535-2962 to ask about the Brazilian or Portuguese groups.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the public parish listing gives a rectory phone number for questions.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come in and sit without signing up. Sunday Masses are in Q'eqchi at 7 am, Spanish at 10 am and English at noon, so pick the one you follow. Confession on Saturdays runs from 3 to 3:45 pm.
first_visit_tips: Choose the Sunday Mass in the language you follow: Q'eqchi at 7 am, Spanish at 10 am, English at noon.
Thursday adoration runs after the 8:30 am Mass and ends at 6:30 pm with the rosary.
The rectory phone is 215-535-2962.

records.notes: Tier 2 is not complete. The parish site (smtparish.org redirects to smtphila.org) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, so its own pages were not read and were not retried. The facts here come from the archdiocese parish listing, read this pass, and from tier 1. Q'eqchi has no two letter code, so it is left out of access.languages. The Portuguese apostolate is named but no language is stated for it, so no language tag was added. research_tier stays 1 because the group's own pages were not read.

records.name: St. Matthew Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Cottman Avenue and Battersby Street in the Northeast with four Sunday Masses, daily Mass, and, according to the archdiocese listing, some liturgies interpreted in American Sign Language.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or volunteer through the rectory. The Marthas meet each Monday morning after the 8:30 am Mass, and lectors, ushers and extraordinary ministers sign up through the rectory. Volunteers need background clearances first.

schedule.text: Saturday Vigil Mass at 4:30 pm. Sunday Masses at 7 am, 9 am, 11 am and 7 pm. Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 6:30 and 8:30 am, and Saturday Mass at 8:30 am. Confession Saturdays 7:45 to 8:15 am and 3 to 4 pm.

access.notes: The archdiocese listing says some liturgies are interpreted in American Sign Language and links to a separate schedule of those Masses. The parish's own pages list no ASL Mass, so confirm with the rectory before you plan around one.

first_step.how: Come to the 9 am or 11 am Sunday Mass, then call the rectory at 215-333-0585 about joining the Marthas (they meet each Monday after the 8:30 am Mass) or another ministry.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the parish lists a rectory phone for groups such as the Marthas and ushers, though it does not say what a first meeting is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come and sit without signing up. Sunday Masses are at 7, 9 and 11 am and 7 pm, and the 11 am Mass is livestreamed on Facebook. Volunteer roles need a PA State Police criminal record check and a PA child abuse history clearance, and the parish has a safe environment coordinator who can help with them.
first_visit_tips: Watch the 11 am Sunday Mass livestream on Facebook first if you want to see how the parish runs before you go.
Ask the rectory about the safe environment coordinator if you want to volunteer; the clearances must be renewed every 5 years.
FBI fingerprint clearance is only needed if you have lived in Pennsylvania for less than 10 years; a disclosure statement is needed if you have lived there 10 years or more.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the parish page links to an ASL schedule. The parish's home page and liturgical groups page list no ASL Mass and no schedule link. The archdiocese listing says some liturgies are interpreted; it was seen only as a search snippet this pass, not read in full. The deaf tag and the access note are kept from tier 1 and flagged for the rectory to confirm. The parish page prints a rectory email on a different domain (stmmayfair.org), which was not recorded. The clearance requirements apply to volunteers, not to people attending Mass. Cost and processing time for the clearances are not stated. The Children's Choir and Altar Servers pages were not read and list no contact on the pages read.

records.name: St. Michael Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 2nd and Jefferson Streets with an English Mass and a Spanish Mass on Sundays, and a weekday Mass in English.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in English or Spanish, or join a ministry. The parish lists a Welcoming and Hospitality ministry, CCD teaching on Tuesdays at 6:30 pm, flower and altar server ministries, and Mission in the Streets on Saturdays. A Legion of Mary group meets Mondays from 6 to 7 pm. Most ministry pages send you to the parish office for details.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 9:30 am in English and 11:30 am in Spanish. Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 8:30 am. Confession Sundays 10:30 to 11:20 am and Thursdays 5 to 6:30 pm, or by appointment. Thursday adoration runs 9 am to 8 pm.

first_step.how: Come to the 9:30 am English or 11:30 am Spanish Sunday Mass, then call the parish office at 215-739-2358 about joining a ministry such as Welcoming and Hospitality or CCD teaching.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the parish lists an office phone and address that its ministry pages point people to.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and you can attend without signing up. Sunday Masses are at 9:30 am in English and 11:30 am in Spanish, and weekday Mass is at 8:30 am. Ministry pages send new people to the parish office rather than to a sign-up form, so calling or visiting the office is the next step.
first_visit_tips: Confession is Sunday 10:30 to 11:20 am and Thursday 5 to 6:30 pm, or by appointment.
The parish office address is 1445 N. 2nd St.
The Legion of Mary meets Mondays from 6 to 7 pm, according to the parish announcements page.

records.notes: Phone: the contact page gives 215-739-2358, which matches tier 1. The home page prints 215.397.2358 for the office, so the two conflict and the contact page number is recorded. The home page lists office hours of Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, 10 am to 1 pm; the contact page lists none, so the hours are not in the record. Cleaning of the Church is 9:30 to 11 am on the home page and 10 am to noon on the ministries page, so no time is recorded. The parish site says nothing about the language of the weekday Mass, so the English in the summary is carried over from tier 1 unverified. The Mission in the Streets and Neocatechumenal Way groups list no contacts. Tier 1 said confession is by appointment; the site lists fixed times as well.

records.name: St. Monica Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 17th and Ritner Streets in South Philadelphia with Sunday Masses at 8:30, 10 and 11:30 am and a Saturday vigil at 5 pm.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or join a parish group. The Senior Citizens Group (ages 55 and up) meets Mondays at 1 pm from September to June in the Senior School cafeteria. Other groups include the Holy Name Society, the St. Vincent de Paul Society, and RCIA for adults who want to join the Church. Call the rectory at 215-334-4170 to ask about any of them.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8:30, 10 and 11:30 am. Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm and Saturday Mass at 8:30 am. Weekday Mass at 6:30 am when school is in session and at 8:30 am. Saturday confession 4 to 4:45 pm. Eucharistic adoration on Mondays 9 am to 3 pm, September to May.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass at 8:30, 10 or 11:30 am, then call the rectory at 215-334-4170 about the Senior Citizens Group or RCIA.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the parish gives a main phone number for groups such as RCIA, though the site has no welcome page.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come to a Sunday service without signing up. The rectory answers questions about groups, and many of them meet from September to June, so fall is a natural time to start.
first_visit_tips: Confession at St. Monica is on Saturdays from 4 to 4:45 pm; at St. Edmond it is the Saturday after First Friday from 3 to 3:45 pm.
Eucharistic adoration at St. Monica runs Mondays from 9 am to 3 pm, September through May.
Call the rectory first to confirm meeting days, since many groups on the site have no listed times.

records.notes: Corrections to tier 1: the site gives Sunday Masses at 8:30 am, not 8 am, and Saturday confession at St. Monica is 4 to 4:45 pm. The parish also worships at St. Edmond (Saturday 4 pm vigil, Sunday 10 am Mass), but no address was found, so it is only mentioned in the text. The calendar page lists no events; its only 2026 date is a daily readings date, so no sign-of-life date was recorded and status stays probably_active. The organizations page names many groups, most with only the rectory number and few with meeting times. The record lists the ones with a clear meeting time or join path.

records.name: St. Nicholas of Tolentine Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 9th and Watkins Streets in South Philadelphia with Sunday Masses at 9 and 11 am and daily morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or ask the rectory about the parish's food cupboard, which takes donations at the rectory office, or about Aid for Friends, where volunteers prepare meals that are picked up and delivered to homebound neighbors. The choir rehearses Wednesdays at 7:45 pm, and a Morning Prayer group meets Monday to Friday at 7:45 am before the 8 am Mass. RCIA for adults and adult Bible study are listed on the parish website.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 9 and 11 am. Weekday and Saturday Mass at 8 am. Saturday Vigil Mass at 5 pm, and a 7 pm vigil for holy days. Holy day Masses at 8 am, noon and 7 pm. Saturday confession 4 to 5 pm.

first_step.how: Come to the 9 am or 11 am Sunday Mass, then call the parish at 215-463-1326 about the RCIA program for adults or the adult Bible study.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the parish lists a phone number and separate pages for RCIA and adult faith formation, but it does not say what a first meeting is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come and sit without signing up. The parish offers Sunday Masses at 9 and 11 am and a weekday Mass at 8 am. The parish also runs RCIA for adults and an adult Bible study and faith formation program, so ask the office which one fits you.
first_visit_tips: Call the parish at 215-463-1326 to ask about groups; the site lists committees but few contact details.
Morning Prayer meets Monday to Friday at 7:45 am, before the 8 am Mass.
The Choir rehearses Wednesdays at 7:45 pm if you sing.

records.notes: Holy day Mass times: the parish page gives 8 am, noon and 7 pm, while tier 1 said 9 am for the midday holy day Mass, so the page's time is used. Zip changed from 19147 to 19148 to match the address printed on the home page (910 Watkins St.). The status and the 2026-10 date rest on the home page link to a bulletin named 2026-10-04 (the festival notice on the same page gives no year). That PDF redirected to another host and was not followed because of the per group fetch limit, so check it before relying on the active status. The festival postponed to Sunday, October 4 is not in the record because its year is not shown in the page text. The social services page also lists a Day Care for children 1 and a half to 4 (215-462-1515) and an after-school program, which are not in this record. Hope in Christ, an archdiocesan addiction support resource named on that page, is a resource rather than a group, so it is not listed as a lead. Saturday confession 4 to 5 pm is carried over from tier 1 and was not on the pages read.

records.name: St. Patrick Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 20th and Locust Streets in Center City with Sunday, weekday and Saturday Masses, a chapel open daily for prayer, and a Thursday Holy Hour.
records.what_you_do: Pray in the Lower Church chapel, which is open most of the day, or come to Night Prayer at 9 pm. Thursday evenings bring a 7 pm Holy Hour with confessions. The parish page describes a young adult group for people in their 20s and 30s that meets Thursday evenings, with adoration and confession at 7 pm and a faith discussion at 8 pm in the parish hall. Becoming Catholic (OCIA) meets Mondays from 7 to 8:30 pm in the Parish Hall, and the parish lists pages for its ministry to the poor, pro-life work and liturgical ministries, though those pages give no details.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 5:15 pm and Saturday Mass at 8 am. Sunday Masses at 8:30 am, 11 am and 6:30 pm. Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 7:30 am and 12:05 pm. Holy Hour with confessions on Thursdays at 7 pm. Confession Fridays at 12:30 pm, Saturdays at 4:30 pm and Sundays at 5:45 pm.

access.notes: A capital campaign plans an elevator and restrooms, with no date given.

first_step.how: Come to any listed Mass or sit in the chapel, then fill out the pre-registration form and return it to the office, or give it to a priest after Mass, if you want to join the parish.
first_step.basis: The join page explains how a new person starts, with a pre-registration form and then a meeting with the parish, and Mass and the chapel need no sign-up; the linked flier's file name includes 2018, so confirm it is current.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come and sit quietly. Masses are held in the Upper Church, and the Lower Church chapel is open most of the day for quiet prayer. If you want to join the parish, the next step after sending in the form is a short visit with the parish to get to know you.
first_visit_tips: Grab a bulletin and hymnal on the way in at the Upper Church.
The church is at 242 S. 20th St., at 20th and Locust.
Call (215) 735-9900 to ask for the current pre-registration form, since the linked flier's file name mentions 2018.

records.notes: Sunday morning confession: the mass times page gives 10:15 or 10:30 am, while tier 1 said 10:30 to 10:50 am; the page's wording is kept in the schedule. Chapel closing is given as 9 pm in one place and 9:20 pm in another, so the record says about 9 pm. Address changed to 242 S. 20th St., printed on the join page. The linked pre-registration flier is named with 2018 in its file name, so the form may be old. The home page dated items (October 8 to 12) have no year in the page text; the file names show 2026 and 2027 but those are not visible text, so no sign-of-life date was recorded. The young adult page's only dates are photo captions from 2020 and 2021, so it is not treated as recent evidence. The women's group page has only a title and the address, so nothing from it is recorded. The parish email is obscured on the site, so it was left out. The OCIA Monday time is taken from the home page.

records.name: St. Paul Parish
records.summary: An Augustinian parish at 923 Christian Street with an active young adult ministry. Its events include a monthly service night, a biweekly Bible study and a young adult Mass with a social afterward.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly service night at the Friary, a project built around the Corporal Works of Mercy (October's project is homelessness), or to the biweekly young adult Bible study. All adults are welcome, married or single, and you can come to one event or many. Email youngadults@stpaulphilly.org or join the St Paul young adult group on WhatsApp to get the next dates.

schedule.text: Monthly service night on a Tuesday at 6:30 pm at the Friary. Young adult Bible study on Wednesdays at 7 pm, held every two weeks at the Friary.

cost.text: The site does not list a cost for these events.

first_step.how: Email youngadults@stpaulphilly.org or join the St Paul young adult group on WhatsApp for the next dates, then come to the next service night or Bible study at the Friary.
first_step.basis: The young adult page says all adults are welcome, married or single, that you can attend one event or many, and lists several ways to get in touch.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Bible study is an evening of scripture, prayer and fellowship at the Friary, held every two weeks on Wednesdays at 7 pm. The monthly service night on a Tuesday at 6:30 pm is a service project, and October's focus is homelessness. The page gives no cost and does not say how long either one runs.
first_visit_tips: Go to the Friary at 808 S. Hutchinson St. for the service night and Bible study, since both meet there rather than at the church.
You can come to one event or many, which the page says, so the first visit does not commit you to anything.
The Homeless Ministry also needs volunteers; the parish asks for emails to office@stpaulphilly.org.

records.notes: Tier 1 put the October 18 Young Adult Mass and social into schedule text and days. That is a dated one time event, so the schedule now gives only the recurring service night and Bible study, and Sunday is removed from days. The October 18 event is still on the young adult page, which supports last_sign_of_life 2026-10 (the page also lists October 13, 14, 21 and 28 dates, all 2026). Cost: the page gives none, so the level is unknown (tier 1 had null). The tier 1 community_fridge interest is kept because nothing read disproves it; homeless_outreach is added because the October service night project is the Homeless Ministry. Parish Masses on the home page: Saturday vigil 5 pm; Sunday 8 am, noon and 5 pm; weekdays 7:30 am. St. Mary Magdalen de Pazzi (712 Montrose St.) has a Sunday 10 am Mass. The Homeless Ministry page lists 2026 outreach dates (blessing bag assembly October 13 at 6:30 pm; lunch assembly October 17 at 9 am and outreach at 9:30 am). Project Nonna visits parishioners who cannot get to church and takes contacts at office@stpaulphilly.org. Both are parish ministries without their own website, so they could become separate records later. The home page also lists a November 15, 2026 event called The Blast, which was not checked. The parish sitemap returned 404, so pages were found through the home page links.

leads_only.name: Aid for Friends
leads_only.note: Named on the St. Nicholas social services page as a free meal and friendship program for homebound people across Greater Philadelphia. The page gives no website for it, so it was not checked.
